posts.title: An Analysis of GrapheneOS's Server Infrastructure
posts.description: I was poking around the GrapheneOS infrastructure repo last week, just curious how they build things. First thing I noticed: every single server runs Arch Linux. DNS nodes, mail servers, the lot. You can verify it directly — every package list includes pacman-contrib and pacutils , which are Arch-specific and don’t exist on any other distro. posts.title: The Reboot Problem: Why Most Operating Systems Can't Defend Against a Compromised Root
posts.description: Assume malware has run on your machine and obtained root. After a reboot, is it still there? For most operating systems the answer is yes. The OS itself offers no structural resistance once root is obtained — it can write to system directories, replace binaries, install kernel modules, modify boot configuration. None of this requires exploiting a vulnerability. It’s just what root can do by design
